name: Euroscepticism
summary: Opposition to, or qualified scepticism about, the European Union and European integration. Hard Euroscepticism rejects the project and wants withdrawal; soft Euroscepticism accepts membership but resists further integration or a federal Europe in the name of national interest and sovereignty. It is held by parties of the right and the left, with right-wing variants adding immigration and identity themes and left-wing ones objecting to neoliberalism and austerity.
scope: Party-based Euroscepticism in the Taggart-Szczerbiak sense, centred on the shared core of sovereignty and anti-federalism, as expressed by Thatcher's Bruges speech, UKIP/Brexit Party, the AfD and similar parties. Because it is a stance on one issue shared by very different parties, most answers outside sovereignty are low-confidence or split; left Euroscepticism (Syriza, Die Linke, Dutch SP) would answer economic statements differently.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Right-wing variants stress national identity while left variants do not; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not part of the Eurosceptic core; right-wing parties often favour it while left Eurosceptics oppose it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not part of the Eurosceptic core; right-wing and left-wing variants take opposite sides.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Right-wing variants lean toward descent, left variants against; not a Eurosceptic core issue.

minority-language-support.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: A stance on European integration spanning left and right; adherents are split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Adherents are split; left Eurosceptics stress economic change while right ones stress sovereignty alone.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not a defining position; adherents are split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The shared core of sovereignty and democratic accountability points against trading freedoms, though not a stated position. Inferred from its principles; no source addresses it directly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Adherents are split: left strands favour global solidarity while right strands prioritise compatriots.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The sovereignty core and the Thatcher-style and AfD-style national-independence strands favour national defence capacity over dependence, though not a stated position. Inferred from its principles; no source addresses it directly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Eurosceptics object to the euro and ECB independence from national democratic control, though right-wing Eurosceptics split on hard money.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents are split and no source treats this as part of it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The precautionary principle is an EU treaty principle that some eurosceptics resist and others accept, so adherents split.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the Thatcherite and national-conservative strand that backs NATO as alliance of sovereign states.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national sovereignty and borders, which opposes non-consensual annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the weight placed on national tradition, which doesn’t favour curbing churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the strand’s attachment to national symbols and institutions such as the monarchy.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Eurosceptic parties are split, since some back regional self-determination while others stress territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Adherents split: the national-interest strand prefers one national legal system, while others favour regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty-and-democracy framing, which has no place for divine rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Right Eurosceptics sometimes favour flat taxes but left ones oppose them, so adherents split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Single-issue stance on the EU takes no position on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the Bruges-speech emphasis on national democracy and rule of law.

space-expansion.rationale: Single-issue stance on the EU takes no position on space expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Single-issue stance on the EU takes no position on mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the democratic-sovereignty framing, which opposes glorifying leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Single-issue stance on the EU takes no position on custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Mainstream Euroscepticism is a sovereignty stance with no socialist doctrine; right variants reject it and left variants rarely endorse the thesis.

land-redistribution.rationale: Right-wing Eurosceptic parties defend property and farmers; left variants are split, so the typical stance is mildly against expropriation.

refugee-return.rationale: Eurosceptics split: some back refugees' return to conflict zones, but they mostly oppose descendants' resettlement claims; no shared position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Euroscepticism defends existing sovereign nation-states and their borders; inferred from that sovereignty core.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Eurosceptic parties across Europe, including the AfD and UKIP, defend liberal freedoms of belief in the West.

women-must-cover.rationale: Right Eurosceptic parties often back burqa or veil bans, the opposite of compelling cover, and left ones also oppose a mandate.

common-currency.rationale: Rejecting the euro and keeping national currencies is a core Eurosceptic position, in hard and soft variants and across the left and right.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Eurosceptics favour national sovereignty over cross-border political unity; inferred from the anti-federalist core.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The sovereignty and national-identity emphasis suggests a unitary national culture; inferred, and not addressed directly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement has no position on minorities' emigration; not addressed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Right-wing variants stress national identity and culture over economic determinism; left variants differ. Inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Left Eurosceptics object to EU competition rules as neoliberal, while free-market ones praise competition; split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Eurosceptics of all kinds attacked the eurozone bailouts, and the AfD was founded in opposition to them.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Eurosceptics typically want elected national parliaments to override the European Court of Justice and the ECHR, a stance Brexit campaigners argued.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Right Eurosceptic parties such as the AfD oppose quotas, and the left variants may favour them; inferred as mildly opposed overall.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Thatcher's Bruges speech and Brexit campaigners favoured free trade with the wider world, not a closed bloc, though left variants are protectionist.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Eurosceptics typically oppose supranational regulation, but left variants favour such standards; mildly negative.

moral-incentives.rationale: No Eurosceptic tradition seeks to replace material incentives; inferred as opposed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Euroscepticism is a parliamentary and electoral movement that seeks withdrawal through referendums and votes.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: UKIP and similar parties are generally monarchist or indifferent to titles; inferred, not addressed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the national-identity and sovereignty themes of right-wing Euroscepticism; left variants are indifferent.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national self-rule and rejection of rule by outside bodies (Bruges speech).

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the national-interest and national-identity emphasis of the soft and right-wing strands.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source ties it to this issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source ties it to this issue.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source ties it to this issue.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Brexiteers invoke the Commonwealth and Anglosphere while other adherents reject imperial nostalgia; split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the Thatcherite and Brexit case for open global trade outside the EU; left Eurosceptics would differ.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source ties it to this issue.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration shared by left and right parties; adherents are split and no source ties it to this issue.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Many right Eurosceptics want to leave the European Convention on Human Rights while others favour a domestic bill of rights; split.

notes: Euroscepticism is defined by one issue, so the profile is thin outside sovereignty and integration. Strands differ: right-wing parties add immigration and identity; left-wing ones object to neoliberalism and austerity; the Brexit era blurred hard and soft by shifting from exit to reform (per ECPS). Primary sources could not be opened in full (margaretthatcher.org blocked), so the Bruges text is taken from quoted passages.
